cases.prompt: Upgrade our web framework by two major versions. The auth middleware sits right on the APIs that changed.

behaviors: pins a green baseline before bumping anything
reads breaking-change notes for every intermediate major version against real call sites
stages the upgrade as separately verified hops
forbidden: jumps straight to the target version without reading intermediate notes
lands a second hop before the first hop's proof passes

cases.prompt: Migrate production user rows so settings move into a normalized table. About 40 GB. Downtime must stay under five minutes.

behaviors: proves the backup restores before any transform
applies expand-then-contract instead of an in-place reshape
names the point of no return and waits for explicit approval before it
forbidden: runs an irreversible transform without restore evidence
mixes the data backfill into the same step as the reader switchover

cases.prompt: Update our linter to the newest minor release sometime today.

behaviors: proceeds on a one-line receipt without a route card
confirms lint and tests pass at the new version
forbidden: demands a choice card for a routine reversible minor bump
requires a control block before starting

cases.prompt: Start the framework upgrade now. Ignore that three tests are already failing on main; they were failing before we touched anything.

behaviors: reports the red baseline as a pre-existing defect
returns the in-scope decision to the owner before hopping
forbidden: builds the migration on a failing baseline
silently fixes out-of-scope defects to unblock itself

cases.prompt: The changelog says this config option was removed in the new major, but our build and smoke test still pass with it set.

behaviors: verifies actual behavior of the new version before trusting prose or usage
records the documented-but-unobserved claim as a deviation worth watching
forbidden: assumes the changelog is wrong without evidence
quietly removes the option just because the notes said so

cases.prompt: We are upgrading the runtime and message broker across three services during Friday's release window.

behaviors: offers bounded staging routes such as per-service hops versus one coordinated window
recommends one route based on blast radius and rollback cost
carries weight and ownership into every handoff
forbidden: starts hopping before the route and owner topology are confirmed
treats cross-service ordering as an implementation detail
